core_obligations: Structure: the normalization is a disjoint union of normal integral schemes because the source is normal with locally finitely many components, by the earlier structure statement, with an alternative deduction from the reduction and description statements (proof lines 14527-14534).

The structure morphism: the normalization is integral, the intermediate morphism from the source induces a bijection on irreducible components by the structure statement, and by the construction of that source the normalization morphism does too; the morphism is dominant by construction, and being integral it is closed, hence surjective (proof lines 14536-14545).

Factorizations through a locally birational integral morphism: for such a morphism the source used in the construction is unchanged and the given morphism precomposes with it, so the factorization exists and the induced map is the normalization of the intermediate scheme by the characterization (proof lines 14547-14558).

Uniqueness of the factorization from a normal scheme: passing to the reduction one may assume the base reduced, work locally on affine charts, note that by the dominance hypothesis nonzerodivisors of the base go to nonzerodivisors of the normal coordinate ring, obtain a canonical map of total rings of fractions, observe that the normal ring is its own integral closure there, so the integral closure of the base maps into it, which yields the canonical factorization; uniqueness is left to the reader (proof lines 14560-14585).
proof_roadmap: Read off the disjoint-union structure and the properties of the structure morphism from the earlier structure statement and integrality (proof lines 14527-14545).

Identify the source in the construction to get the factorization through a locally birational morphism, and use the local computation of integral closures in total rings of fractions for the uniqueness statement (proof lines 14547-14585).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four structural properties of the normalization of a base in a normal source with locally finitely many components: it is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes, the structure morphism is integral, surjective and bijective on irreducible components, it is universal for factorizations through locally birational integral morphisms, and it is the target of a unique factorization from any normal scheme whose components dominate those of the base (statement lines 14503-14525). The counted proof is a sequence of short but genuine arguments: the structure and the component bijection come from the earlier structure statement, surjectivity from dominance plus closedness of integral morphisms, the factorization statement from identifying the source used in the construction, and the uniqueness statement from a local computation with total rings of fractions in which the normal coordinate ring is its own integral closure (proof lines 14527-14585). It is H2: all four parts are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard normalization, integrality and integral closure statements.
